name: manual_e91d40
claim: When a shared condition gates two logically-independent checks (e.g. "skip check A" reusing the same boolean that correctly gates "skip check B"), a scenario that legitimately satisfies the shared condition for check A will silently also skip check B, even though check B has no relationship to why the exemption exists. Before reusing an existing exemption/skip condition for a new check, ask whether the new check's OWN reason for existing has anything to do with the original exemption's reason -- if not, it needs its own independent condition, not a shared one.
